seo.description: Open a Beancount ledger as read-only SQL tables of transactions, postings, balances and metadata, follow its includes, and run BQL through rledger.

og.title: Query a Beancount ledger with SQL

header.title: Beancount client
header.lead: Query a ledger as read-only SQL tables, or with BQL through rledger, and edit it in your own text editor.

bands.title: Open a ledger
text: Install rledger or Python Beancount. rledger takes precedence when both are there, and only rledger supports BQL and validation output in diagnostics.

Choose a ledger with Browse… or open a .beancount file from Finder: the path is the whole connection, and beancount:///path/to/main.beancount URLs can be imported. An app opened from Finder does not inherit your shell’s PATH, so if the backend runs in Terminal but not here, name it with launchctl setenv TABLEPRO_RUSTLEDGER_BINARY or TABLEPRO_BEANCOUNT_PYTHON and relaunch.

The Python backend runs the plugins that ship with Beancount and skips any other plugin directive, which is third-party code, until you turn on Run Ledger Plugins for that connection. Skipped plugins are listed in diagnostics.

bands.title: Query the ledger
text: Transactions, postings, accounts, balances, prices, directives, metadata and source files are tables: join postings to transactions on transaction_id, and accounts by name. Amounts arrive booked, with arithmetic, costs and prices resolved, and posting costs and inline prices in their own columns.

Transactions, postings and several directive tables carry a source_location such as main.beancount:42, so a row leads back to its line. Prefix a query with BQL: to send it to rledger; browsing, row counts and paging work on the result, SQL parameters do not.

include directives are followed, literal paths and globs alike, and every ledger file and referenced document is watched, so the next query reads a saved change without reconnecting. The connection is always at Safe Mode Read-Only: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and schema changes are refused.

moveData: <export>Export</export> a table or a query result as {exportFormats}. <files>Other files TablePro opens as databases</files> include SQLite, DuckDB and Parquet.

faq.question: Does a ledger with errors still open?
faq.answer: Through rledger, yes. The ledger is projected even when validation fails, and each problem is a row in diagnostics with its file, line, severity and message.

faq.question: Can one connection open several ledgers?
faq.answer: One connection is one ledger file, with no switching. A main file that includes the others brings them all in, globs included.
